clue.text: Gorge, mostly mad with energy

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for mad is dropped

parts.note: raving means wildly mad
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone gorges themselves in a frenzy, fuelled by manic energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' reads as a verb for overeating, but it is the noun for a steep valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravine is a deep narrow valley, a close synonym of a gorge.

clue.text: Ship docks in empty port over here

indicators.note: a ship that docks goes into a harbour, so these letters go inside the others
an empty word has had its contents removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of port
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship pulls into a deserted harbour while someone calls out to attract attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship's letters sit inside the shell of port: P, SS, T.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered interjection is used to catch someone's attention discreetly, like calling 'over here'.

clue.text: Surprisingly copy him, red under the skin

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not in the expected order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A surprising instruction to imitate a man who has gone red beneath his skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypodermic is the medical adjective for what lies or is injected beneath the skin.

clue.text: Supporting number to accommodate one part of diet

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece is housed inside another

parts.note: ten is a number
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A backing number in a show makes room for one more part of the regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is any numeral, not a song; the one goes into the numeral, not into the supporting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is one of the main nutrient groups making up a balanced diet.

clue.text: War vehicle's function: kill, primarily

parts.note: tan is the abbreviation for the tangent function in trigonometry

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of kill

explanation.surface: The purpose of a war machine is, above all, to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests purpose, but here it is the trigonometric function, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank is an armoured tracked military vehicle.

clue.text: Flee Tahiti hotel with girl, run away excited

indicators.note: excited letters are agitated and jumbled out of their order
run is abbreviated to one letter, and away tells us that letter leaves the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H
taken as written, before R for run is removed

explanation.surface: A man runs off excitedly from a Tahitian hotel with a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away' looks like a second definition, but it removes R (run) from girl to leave GIL for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To hightail it is an informal idiom for leaving in a great hurry, that is, to flee.

clue.text: Saturate large part of battlefield ending in bog

indicators.note: a large part is not the whole, so the final letter of the battle site is dropped

parts.note: Waterloo is the Belgian battlefield where Napoleon was defeated

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter, which is the one taken

parts.note: the last letter of bog

explanation.surface: Much of a battlefield is drenched and ends up a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: To waterlog something is to soak it so thoroughly that it can hold no more water.

clue.text: Sailors wasting five years at sea? They probably won't agree!

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular noun: one of those who probably won't agree

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the Roman five is lost from the word for sailors

parts.note: the navy is the body of sailors
V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors spend years at sea and come back disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: V is removed from NAVY to leave NAY, then the letters of years are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A naysayer habitually objects or denies, so is someone unlikely to agree.

clue.text: Beast that's fussy I'm breaking in

indicators.note: breaking in means forcing an entry, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: anal is informal for obsessively fussy
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A trainer complains about a picky beast he is breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking in' sounds like taming a horse, but it signals one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is a non-human creature, which is what an animal is.

clue.text: Bar writer pens two fifths of story

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writing instrument

indicators.note: of a five-letter word, two fifths means just two of its letters, here the opening pair

parts.note: the first two of story's five letters

explanation.surface: An author in a bar jots down part of a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is a pen, not an author; Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant or wine bar.

clue.text: Laughed introducing a king? Be careful!

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so the new letters are put inside

parts.note: teheed means laughed with a tee-hee, a giggle
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A courtier giggles while presenting a monarch, and gets a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heed is to pay attention, an idiom equivalent to being careful.

clue.text: Sadly I regret drinking French wine, recovering

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one piece swallows the other
something sadly done is done badly, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A drinker confesses regret about French wine while getting over a hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrieving is getting something back, a synonym for recovering it.

clue.text: Before end of symphony, loser turns up gripping instrument with determination

indicators.note: gripping means holding tight, so one piece is held inside another
in a down clue turning up means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
the lute is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of symphony

explanation.surface: Before a symphony ends, the losing player turns up clutching his instrument, determined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the built piece ahead of the Y from symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolutely means in a firm, unwavering way, the adverb for acting with determination.

clue.text: Joke about face of ruthless islander, heartless as a giant

indicators.note: about means around, so the joke goes round the selected letter

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of ruthless

indicators.note: with no heart, the middle letters of the word are taken out

parts.note: an Antiguan is someone from the Caribbean island of Antigua

explanation.surface: A merciless islander with no heart makes a joke about being as big as a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: IG, the two central letters of ANTIGUAN, are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantuan means enormous, the same as the adjective giant; the word comes from Rabelais's giant Gargantua.

clue.text: Some tea blend's strong enough

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the answer is a run of letters inside the next words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A particular mix of tea is robust enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able means having the capacity or strength to do something, so strong enough.

clue.text: Drain part of eye, admitting problem

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece is let inside the other

parts.note: cones are light-sensitive cells in the retina
a sum is a maths problem

explanation.surface: A medic drains part of the eye, admitting there is a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume something is to use it up, as to drain resources.

clue.text: Aware of Cockney's hide and seek tactic?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops initial H sounds, so the words are said in that London accent

parts.note: the tactic in hide and seek is to hope and hide, said without the H sounds

explanation.surface: A Londoner explains the strategy for a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: The seeker's quarry must hope and hide; a Cockney says this with dropped aitches and a run-together 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open-eyed means being watchful and alert, so aware of what is going on.

clue.text: Attempt to claim one record that's in three parts

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun: something that's in three parts

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral one
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone tries for a record-breaking three-part attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilogy is a set of three related works, so it comes in three parts.

clue.text: I speak angrily about working for a period of time

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the angry word goes round the other

parts.note: to rage is to speak in fury
on means functioning or working

explanation.surface: Someone rants about having to work for a long stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is an archaeological era, the period when iron tools came into use.

clue.text: Close predator

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a marine mammal that hunts fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like an adjective meaning nearby, suggesting a lurking hunter; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means to fasten something shut and also names the fish-eating marine mammal.

clue.text: Present caught rabbit cake

indicators.note: caught here means heard, so the word is identified by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: current means present, of now
bun is a dialect pet name for a rabbit

explanation.surface: A gift of a captured rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: A currant bun is a sweet bread roll studded with dried fruit, a British teatime staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant bun is a small sweet bake, which counts as a type of cake.

clue.text: Performing in duet without restraint

indicators.note: letters that are performing are put through their paces in a new order

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Two musicians perform a duet freely and without inhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untied has had its bonds loosened, so is free of restraint.

clue.text: Form bad pathogen

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoilt and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dangerous strain of germ develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a verb for germs developing, but it is the noun for a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptagon is a seven-sided shape, an example of a geometric form.

clue.text: Dull lawyer gives up part-way through

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read from bottom to top
part-way through means starting inside the words, so the answer sits within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of lawyer and start of gives

explanation.surface: A boring solicitor abandons a case halfway through.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes something drab and uninteresting, a synonym for dull.

clue.text: Where pigs presumably go to sleep warm

parts.note: pigs head off to a place: to a
a sty is where pigs are kept and sleep

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about where pigs bed down when they want to be cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as TO A STY: pigs presumably go to a sty to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal word for comfortably warm.

clue.text: American to drink deeply (but not very loud) water

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the musical marking is removed from the drinking verb

parts.note: to quaff is to drink heartily
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: An American gulps water, but quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is the Latin word for water, used in English for water in names and labels.

clue.text: Item of footwear that is in good condition swapped

indicators.note: swapped means the two pieces change places, so the second comes first

parts.note: well means healthy
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A shoe that is in good condition gets exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives IE then WELL; swapped puts WELL first. A wellie is a rubber Wellington boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie is a waterproof rubber boot, so an item of footwear.

clue.text: Large sun scattered particles

indicators.note: scattered things are spread about in no order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A giant star sends out a scatter of tiny bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Granules are small grains, so they are tiny particles.
